sources.quote: A charter student (and one of the most esteemed) of W. A. Hofmann at the Royal College of Chemistry, Abel left the college in 1851...
Abel left the college in 1851 to take a post as Demonstrator of Chemistry at St. Bartholomew's Hospital, London.
Two years later he secured the position of Lecturer in Chemistry at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich...
Scientific Advisor to the War Office (1854), a position soon elevated to 'Chemist of the War Department'.
Over a decade, starting in 1868, in tandem with Andrew Noble, a polymath in gunnery and munitions, Abel pursued research on the function of gunpowder...
Abel himself came out of retirement to devise one of the best, 'cordite,' in collaboration with James Dewar.
